metrics.description: Fraction of required word-level functional behavior (sum = a+b+c+d) correctly reproduced across the full randomized+corner-case test vector suite; computed as (# vectors matching)/(# vectors applied).
metrics.name: word_recovery_rate

metrics.description: Binary/graded score indicating whether the submission passes the SR1 non-recovery structural gate (i.e. is genuinely word-level recovered RTL rather than a disguised copy of the flattened netlist or a wrapper around its primitives).
metrics.name: structural_match_accuracy

metrics.description: Overall PASS/FAIL verdict: 1 if 100% of test vectors match between recovered_design and the reference flattened netlist AND compilation succeeds AND SR1 structural gate passes; 0 otherwise.
metrics.name: functional_equivalence

acceptance_criteria: evaluate.py compiles submission/recovered_rtl.v together with a generated testbench and inputs/flattened_netlist.v using iverilog, targeting both recovered_design and the reference module.

The testbench applies at least 2000 randomized 4x16-bit input vectors plus the two known vectors from FR2 and all-zero/all-max corner cases, comparing sum outputs from recovered_design against flattened_netlist.v bit-for-bit each cycle.
PASS requires 100% match across all applied vectors between recovered_design output and reference netlist output, plus successful compilation and no fail-on-presence structural violations (SR1).

A naive/empty baseline submission (e.g. a stub module returning sum=0 or an unmodified copy of flattened_netlist.v) must FAIL: the zero-stub fails functional equivalence, and the copied-netlist fails the SR1 non-recovery structural gate.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The flattened netlist implements a 32-bit adder tree computing sum = a + b + c + d over four 16-bit unsigned inputs, structured internally as ((a+b) + (c+d)) but flattened to primitive gates with obfuscated net names so the word-level adder-tree structure is not visible from the netlist alone.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static text scan of submission for instantiation of primitive cell module names (e.g. FA1, XOR2, AND2 from primitive_cells.v) or `include of flattened_netlist.v; if found in bulk (heuristic threshold on gate-primitive instance count), flag as fail-on-presence 'non-recovery' violation regardless of simulation pass, since this indicates the participant sidestepped analysis rather than recovering RTL. This is a supplementary structural gate, never the sole basis for PASS.
security_requirements.requirement: The evaluator must not accept a submission that merely instantiates or textually copies inputs/flattened_netlist.v (which would trivially pass I/O equivalence without demonstrating recovery); evaluate.py performs a structural check that recovered_rtl.v does not include/instantiate the primitive gate modules defined in primitive_cells.v and is not byte-identical or near-identical (e.g. via gate-count heuristics) to flattened_netlist.v.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check that submission does not use non-standard delay constructs (#) that could indicate deliberate timing obfuscation mirroring the original; flag via regex scan for delay control statements, informational only.
security_requirements.requirement: The recovered design must not leak timing-dependent side channels that could reveal internal carry-chain structure through simulation delays (not applicable to combinational functional grading but tracked for completeness in case of gate-level submissions).

hidden_spec.threat_model: The design is delivered as a flattened, gate-level netlist with all hierarchy and meaningful signal names stripped, hiding the word-level arithmetic (adder tree) intent. An adversary or engineer inspecting the netlist cannot easily discern that it is a 4-operand adder tree without behavioral/structural analysis; the goal is to test whether a participant can recover correct word-level semantics purely from black-box/gray-box analysis rather than assuming any word boundaries.

constraints: Do not modify inputs/flattened_netlist.v or any other file under inputs/; only submission/recovered_rtl.v is graded.
The submission file must be self-contained (single file, no includes of other project files).
The recovered module name and port list must match the interface exactly, or the harness cannot instantiate it and the submission fails.
Only standard, freely available toolchain components (iverilog, vvp, yosys) may be assumed; no proprietary EDA tools.
expected_outputs: A single Verilog file submission/recovered_rtl.v defining module recovered_design with the pinned port list, implementing word-level RTL that is behaviorally (I/O) equivalent to inputs/flattened_netlist.v for every possible input vector, verified by exhaustive/randomized simulation against a generated testbench.

functional_requirements.requirement: recovered_design must compute sum = a + b + c + d (unsigned 32-bit result of adding all four 16-bit operands) for every combination of inputs, matching inputs/flattened_netlist.v output bit-for-bit.

For the specific known vectors a=16'h0001,b=16'h0002,c=16'h0003,d=16'h0004 the output sum must equal 32'h0000000A; for a=16'hFFFF,b=16'hFFFF,c=16'hFFFF,d=16'hFFFF the output sum must equal 32'h0003FFFC.
The submitted file must compile cleanly with iverilog (no syntax errors) and simulate with vvp without runtime errors, instantiated with the exact port list given in the interface section.

The recovered RTL must be purely combinational (no clock/reset ports, no latches, output must be a function of only a,b,c,d) and must not merely instantiate or wrap the original flattened netlist file.

public_spec.interface: The recovered design MUST be provided in file submission/recovered_rtl.v and MUST define exactly one top-level module named `recovered_design` with this exact port list: `module recovered_design(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input [15:0] c, input [15:0] d, output [31:0] sum);`. Ports: a, b, c, d are four independent unsigned 16-bit input operands (public, no secrets). sum is the unsigned 32-bit output result. No clock or reset ports are used (the design is purely combinational). The same port list and module name are used by inputs/flattened_netlist.v so the harness can instantiate both modules in one testbench and compare outputs cycle-by-cycle (i.e. per input vector) using $monitor/assert style comparison. The submission file must be synthesizable/simulatable standalone (no external dependencies besides standard Verilog).
public_spec.objective: You are given a flattened, gate-level Verilog netlist (produced by a synthesis/obfuscation flow) that implements some combinational arithmetic function over four 16-bit input buses and produces a single output bus. The netlist has been flattened into primitive gates (AND/OR/XOR/NOT/full-adder-like structures) and all original signal names have been stripped or renamed to generic net labels (e.g. n123, n124...), destroying the original word-level structure. Your task is to analyze the netlist, recover its word-level arithmetic intent, and produce a clean, synthesizable, word-level Verilog RTL module that is functionally equivalent (bit-exact, for all input combinations) to the original flattened design. Submit your recovered RTL as a single self-contained Verilog file.
public_spec.response_format: A single file at submission/recovered_rtl.v containing valid Verilog-2001 (or SystemVerilog subset supported by iverilog) source defining module recovered_design(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input [15:0] c, input [15:0] d, output [31:0] sum); No other files are graded.

title: Recover an adder tree from a flattened netlist
